title: Day 40 and faulty: the 30-day return window against the 24-month warranty
setup: Mr Toad's Boombox Mini (ORD-20124, delivered 14 Oct, 40 days ago) has now stopped charging. He wants a refund. The 30-day change-of-mind window has passed, and the 30-day legal reject window too, but the Boombox Mini has a 24-month warranty (to 14 October 2028), so the right route is a free warranty repair request. A repair request is not a refund and must not be described as one.
turns: My Boombox Mini has stopped charging. I want my money back. ORD-20124, mr.toad@example.com

expected.answer: Explains a refund for change of mind is not available after 30 days (delivered 14 October, 40 days ago), but a fault is covered by the 24-month warranty. Creates a repair request, with a free label both ways, and does not promise a refund or a replacement.
must_not_say: your refund is on its way

criteria: Gets the warranty route from the rules, not from sympathy
Keeps the refund refusal and the repair offer clearly separate

title: Melted Ice by Post is not a fault, and food cannot be returned
setup: Story 11. Pip's Ice by Post (ORD-20160, £16 plus £8.95 Cold delivery) missed Friday and was re-delivered at 08:40 today (shipment note). It has melted. Policy: the page says we cannot promise it is still frozen, melting alone is not a fault, and Ice by Post cannot be returned for change of mind. A torn bag, leak or wrong item would be a fault: tell us within 24 hours with a photo. He gives no such fault, so there is no refund.
turns: My Ice by Post has completely melted. I want a refund. ORD-20160, pip@example.com

expected.answer: Sorry it arrived melted. Explains the product page says we cannot promise it is still frozen and melting alone is not a fault, so no refund on that basis. If the bag was torn, the parcel leaked or it was the wrong item, that is a fault: send a photo within 24 hours of delivery and it can be reported. Offers a person if he wants to take it further.
must_not_say: you will get a full refund

criteria: Kind but does not bend the rule
Tells him exactly what would count as a fault

title: Cancel only the item that is waiting, but the order is already part dispatched
setup: Story 20. Cinderella's ORD-20162 has a Boombox Mini Case (in transit, £19) and a Trophy (£24, out of stock until 7 Dec). The order is part_dispatched, so it cannot be cancelled or changed. She wants to cancel only the Trophy and keep the case. The rule: once packed, it can only be cancelled by returning it once it arrives, within 14 days of delivery. The assistant explains and does not cancel.
turns: I don't want to wait till December for the trophy. Cancel that and just send me the case. ORD-20162, cinderella@example.com

expected.answer: Explains the order is already part dispatched so it cannot be cancelled or changed, including the Trophy. The Trophy is out of stock until 7 December. Options: wait, or return the items once they arrive within the return window for the usual refund terms. Does not cancel and does not promise a different date.

criteria: Does not say it cancelled anything
Offers what is allowed instead of just refusing

title: Part return of a free-delivery order
setup: Jo's ORD-20148 (Daypack £129 and Laptop Sleeve £24, £153, free delivery over £50) was delivered 18 Nov. She wants to return only the Daypack and worries the remaining £24 means delivery gets charged. It does not: delivery was free and is not refunded or charged on a part return. Change of mind: refund £129 less the £2.95 label, £126.05.
turns: If I send back just the Daypack will you charge me for the delivery because the sleeve is under £50? ORD-20148, jo.march@example.com
Ok then, go ahead and return the bag.

expected.answer: No delivery charge is added to her. Delivery was free and a part return does not change that. Creates the return for the Daypack only, refund £126.05 (£129 less £2.95 for the label), paid within 5 working days of the parcel arriving and passing inspection.
must_not_say: we will charge you for delivery

criteria: Returns only the Daypack, not the sleeve
